title: Arnold Wiley, the Arkansas pianist
summary: Williams describes Wiley, from Arkansas, as a superb pianist who played everything and who came to Chicago in the late 1920s. He recalls his song about 35th and State.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you know Arnold Wiley? Yes, I knew him.

Yeah? He's from Arkansas. He's the last time I was in Detroit. My boy, the hell of a piano player, Arnold Wiley. Look skinned, fella. Talked real soft. A little bit of head, light brown, chin light at me. Arnold Wiley, do I know him? He's from Arkansas.
Yeah, he's from Arkansas. Yeah, he's from Arkansas.

Yeah, really. And he had a wife who was in show business too. He's still living. He was, last time I saw his picture in the colored paper, The Defender, Chicago Defender. Oh, that's been many years ago. And I thought he was dead, but he was in Detroit. Arnold Wiley.
When was he in Detroit? Maybe he's still...
Oh, I can't tell you. This is my big friend, 20 years ago I saw his picture in The Defender.
Oh, yeah.
Oh, yeah. Now, I don't know if he's dead or dead, but Arnold Wiley, I know why. Oh, yeah.
Do you know when he came to Chicago? He came to Chicago around the 20s, late 20s. You were earlier in Chicago than he? Yeah.
I know when he come here. Coming here from the Havana, Arkansas.
Directly from Havana, Arkansas. That's right. Arnold Wiley.
A hell of a piano player. Was the older...
He played everything.

Everything. Not just blues. Not just blues. He played everything. He made a number, he ain't going... I'm not coming back to 35th and State no more. He made that number. Yeah. I'm not going back to 35th and State no more.
Oh, yeah. And was he older than you?
Yeah, I don't know how to live a few years old. Three years old. Oh, yeah. That's really interesting. Arnold Wiley and his wife. His little wife was a dancer. Forget her name.
Did she sing also?
I think she sang. Yeah, she sang. Arnold Wiley. Boy, he could play. He could play. I don't mean just blues anything.
Yeah.
Siloquin, all them hard numbers. Arnold Wiley. He might catch him around Detroit. That's the last time I seen the paper. He had his picture. Hmm. You got a picture of him?
No, but I got his records in this book here.
He made a record here. I'm not going back to 35th and State no more.
Let me see.
